name: Hearing Ellipsoids
description: We present a computational benchmark for large Dirichlet eigenvalue spectra on triaxial ellipsoids, comparing finite-element discretizations combined with ARPACK, inertia-based spectrum slicing (SLEPc/MUMPS), a stretched spectral Galerkin (SSG) method, and a multi-probe block-Hankel filter diagonalization that we extend here from a landmark detector into a gap-free complete-spectrum solver. Rather than ranking methods by runtime alone, we ask whether the resulting spectra preserve reliable geometric information. The unit ball serves as a quality-assurance case, since its eigenvalues are known in closed form; for the triaxial case a=1, b=1.5, c=2.3 we add a reverse-geometry validation based on the three-term Weyl law, reconstructing volume, surface area, and integrated mean curvature from finite spectral segments. As the eigenvalue index grows, the error is increasingly dominated by the mesh rather than by the eigensolver. SSG gives the strongest geometric consistency in our tests, reconstructing the volume to about 0.025%. The block-Hankel method extended by a Weyl-equal-count tiling, an analytic one-sided bandpass, and coprime decimation voting produces a complete ordered spectrum of 2034 levels including multiplicities; spectrum slicing returns the same 2034 levels on the identical matrices in 4.9 core-hours against roughly 69,400. For this task, the established method is therefore superior by four orders of magnitude, and we report that plainly.
